before.title: Polarization of a transverse plane wave: linear, circular and elliptical traces, and handedness
before.statement: Let $(E,B)$ be a plane-wave pair of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with wavevector $k\ne0$, angular frequency $\omega>0$ and complex amplitudes $e,b$, and suppose the amplitude conditions of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] hold, so that $|k|=\omega/c$, $k\cdot e=0$ and $b=k\times e/\omega$. This item is a classification definition for that class of transverse plane waves; it adds no field-theoretic content. Write $e=a+id$ with the real vectors $a=\operatorname{Re}e$, $d=\operatorname{Im}e$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]), so that $k\cdot a=k\cdot d=0$; let $\hat k=k/|k|$, and use $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ and $\times$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. Then: (a) [Trace] At fixed $x$ the electric vector is $E(x,t)=a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta$ with $\theta=k\cdot x-\omega t$, and the curve $\gamma(\theta):=a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta$ lies in the transverse plane $k^\perp=\{v: k\cdot v=0\}$. It is the image of the unit circle under the linear map $(u_1,u_2)\mapsto u_1a-u_2d$, it is closed with period $T=2\pi/\omega$, and $\gamma(\theta+\pi)=-\gamma(\theta)$. It is called the **polarisation trace** at $x$; the classification below is independent of $x$. (b) [Classification] (i) **Linear polarisation**: $\dim_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{span}\{a,d\}\le1$; the trace is a segment of the line $\mathbb Ra$ traversed twice per period, and $a=d=0$ is the zero wave. (ii) **Circular polarisation**: $|a|=|d|>0$ and $\langle a,d\rangle=0$; the trace is the circle of radius $|a|$ in $k^\perp$, and $|E(x,t)|=|a|$ for all $(x,t)$. (iii) **Elliptical (nondegenerate, noncircular) polarisation**: $\dim\operatorname{span}\{a,d\}=2$ and not (ii); the trace is a nondegenerate ellipse centred at $0$ with the origin in its interior. If $\langle a,d\rangle=0$, the parametrisation is along principal axes and the semiaxes have lengths $|a|$ and $|d|$; the general principal-axis computation is not asserted by this item. (c) [Handedness] For $a,d\in k^\perp$ the cross product $a\times d$ is parallel to $\hat k$, so the **helicity sign** $H:=\langle a\times d,\hat k\rangle\in\mathbb R$ vanishes exactly in the linear case (i) and is nonzero otherwise ([[def-real-order]] for its sign). This library calls the polarisation **right-handed** when $H<0$ and **left-handed** when $H>0$. Geometrically, $H<0$ means the electric vector at fixed $x$ rotates counterclockwise as seen by an observer facing the incoming wave (looking along $-\hat k$), and $H>0$ means clockwise. This fixes the sign convention of the cited treatment (there: $E_0=\alpha-i\beta$, right-handed iff $\beta=\hat k\times\alpha$, which under $a=\alpha$, $d=-\beta$ is $H=-|a|^2<0$ in the circular case). after.statement: Let $(E,B)$ be a plane-wave pair of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with wavevector $k\ne0$, angular frequency $\omega>0$ and complex amplitudes $e,b$, and suppose the amplitude conditions of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] hold, so that $k\cdot e=0$ and $b=k\times e/\omega$. This item is a classification definition for that class of transverse plane waves; it adds no field-theoretic content. Write $e=a+id$ with the real vectors $a=\operatorname{Re}e$, $d=\operatorname{Im}e$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]), so that $k\cdot a=k\cdot d=0$; let $\hat k=k/|k|$, and use $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ and $\times$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. It is the image of the unit circle under the linear map $(u_1,u_2)\mapsto u_1a-u_2d$, it is closed with phase-parameter period $2\pi$, while $t\mapsto E(x,t)$ has time period $T=2\pi/\omega$, and $\gamma(\theta+\pi)=-\gamma(\theta)$. It is called the **polarisation trace** at $x$; the classification below is independent of $x$. (b) [Classification] (i) **Linear polarisation**: $\dim_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{span}\{a,d\}\le1$; when $\dim\operatorname{span}\{a,d\}=1$, the trace is a nontrivial segment in that span traversed twice per period; when $a=d=0$, the trace is the single point $\{0\}$ and the fields are the zero wave. before.title: Constrained smooth vacuum Maxwell initial-value theory with finite propagation
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]]. Let $t_0<T$ be real, let $E_0,B_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^\infty$ fields ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) on the whole-space laboratory region $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and assume the constraints $$\operatorname{div}E_0=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B_0=0$$ on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). Put $\dot E_0:=c^2\operatorname{curl}B_0$ and $\dot B_0:=-\operatorname{curl}E_0$. No decay, boundedness, compactness or finite-energy hypothesis is imposed on the data. Then: (a) [Existence and explicit representation] There are jointly $C^\infty$ fields $E,B:\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R^3$ (in the extension sense of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]]) satisfying the four smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$, $J\equiv0$ and the initial conditions $E(\cdot,t_0)=E_0$, $B(\cdot,t_0)=B_0$, $\partial_tE(\cdot,t_0)=\dot E_0$, $\partial_tB(\cdot,t_0)=\dot B_0$. Explicitly, each component $E_i$ is the scalar solution $u$ of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](a) with data $(a,b)=(E_{0,i},\dot E_{0,i})$ and $h=0$, each $B_i$ that with $(a,b)=(B_{0,i},\dot B_{0,i})$, in the spherical-mean representation $u=\partial_sH_a+H_b$ of that theorem (the mean being that of [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]). (b) [Uniqueness] Every pair of jointly $C^2$ fields on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (in the extension sense) satisfying the same four equations with $\rho\equiv0$, $J\equiv0$ and $E'(\cdot,t_0)=E_0$, $B'(\cdot,t_0)=B_0$ equals $(E,B)$; the time derivatives at $t_0$ are then automatically $\dot E_0,\dot B_0$ by the Ampere and Faraday equations. (c) [Finite propagation and domain of dependence] If a second pair of constrained data $(E_0',B_0')$ agrees with $(E_0,B_0)$ together with all curls on the closed ball $\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ — that is, $E_0=E_0'$, $B_0=B_0'$, $\operatorname{curl}E_0=\operatorname{curl}E_0'$ and $\operatorname{curl}B_0=\operatorname{curl}B_0'$ there — then the corresponding solutions agree at $(x_*,t_*)$, for all $x_*\in\mathbb R^3$ and $t_*\in[t_0,T]$. Consequently the value at $(x_*,t_*)$ is determined by the Cauchy data on the closed backward cone $K(x_*,t_*)=\{(y,v):|y-x_*|\le c(t_*-v)\}$ of [[def-forward-and-backward-wave-cones-domain-of-dependence-and-influence]]. In the causal geometry of the adopted affine Minkowski model this cone is the model's causal past cone of the event $(x_*,t_*)$ in the chart $x^0=ct$; by the reachability objects of [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]] and the straight-segment criterion and time monotonicity of [[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]], events outside it cannot be joined to $(x_*,t_*)$ by a future causal path, so the constructed field supplies no vacuum influence outside the model's causal cones; this identification of the PDE cone with the model's causal cone is the modelling statement of the item, not an additional empirical claim. (d) [Compact support] If in addition $E_0$ and $B_0$ vanish off a compact set $K\subset\mathbb R^3$, choose $\rho>0$ with $K\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)$ ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]); then for every $t\in[t_0,T]$ one has $E(x,t)=B(x,t)=0$ whenever $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$. (e) [Scope] This is the smooth whole-space vacuum branch with initially constraint-satisfying data; no finite-total-energy conclusion is drawn (a general smooth but non-decaying solution may have infinite total energy), and no boundary condition, inhomogeneous source, weak-branch content or empirical claim is asserted. The result is conditional on the adopted postulates and on $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the latter used only through the cited scalar theorem.
before.strategy: Set $\dot E_0=c^2\operatorname{curl}B_0$, $\dot B_0=-\operatorname{curl}E_0$, and solve the six scalar Cauchy problems by [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](a) with data $(E_{0,i},\dot E_{0,i})$ and $(B_{0,i},\dot B_{0,i})$; the $C^\infty$ claim and the explicit representation through the spherical-mean family $H_\varphi=sM_{cs}\varphi$ are clause (a) of that theorem, whose mean is that of [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]. Put $R_i:=\partial_tE_i-c^2(\operatorname{curl}B)_i$ and $Q_i:=\partial_tB_i+(\operatorname{curl}E)_i$. Each is $C^\infty$ and solves the homogeneous scalar wave equation: differentiating the component wave equations and commuting derivatives ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) gives $\partial_t^2R_i=c^2\Delta R_i$, $\partial_t^2Q_i=c^2\Delta Q_i$. The uniqueness clause [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](b) applied to the zero wave problem gives $R=Q=0$, i.e. the two evolution equations. Clause (d) applies [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](d) to each component, whose data vanish off $K$ because $E_0,B_0$ and their curls do. before.title: Period-averaged energy density, Poynting vector and momentum flux of a plane wave
before.statement: Let $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega>0$ with $\omega=c|k|$, let $e\in\mathbb C^3$ with $k\cdot e=0$ and $b=k\times e/\omega$, and let $(E,B)$ be the corresponding plane-wave solution of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]) on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. Let $u$ and $S$ be the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and $g=S/c^2$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$ the momentum density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Write $T=2\pi/\omega$, $|e|^2=e\cdot\overline e$, $\hat k=k/|k|$, and let $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(x,s)\,ds$ be the period average at fixed $x$. Then, for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$: (a) [Averaged energy density] $\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|e|^2$, independent of $x$ and of the starting time. before.title: Superposition intensity and the coherent interference cross term
before.statement: Let $\omega>0$ and let $k_1,k_2\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ satisfy $|k_1|=|k_2|=\omega/c$. For $j=1,2$ let $e_j\in\mathbb C^3$ with $k_j\cdot e_j=0$, put $b_j=k_j\times e_j/\omega$ and let $(E_j,B_j)$ be the plane-wave solutions of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] given by [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]. Let $a_1,a_2\in\mathbb R$ and put $(E,B):=a_1(E_1,B_1)+a_2(E_2,B_2)$. Then: (a) [Superposition] $(E,B)$ is a smooth source-free solution of the vacuum Maxwell equations ([[pthm-em-linear-superposition]]), and at each fixed $x$ it can be written with a single phase, $$E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\alpha(x)\,e^{i(k_1\cdot x-\omega t)}),\qquad B(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\beta(x)\,e^{i(k_1\cdot x-\omega t)}),$$ where $\alpha(x):=a_1e_1+a_2e_2e^{i\delta(x)}$, $\beta(x):=a_1b_1+a_2b_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ and $\delta(x):=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x$; constant relative phases are absorbed in $e_2$. (b) [Averaged energy density with the coherent cross term] For every $x$, $$\langle u\rangle(x)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{4}|\alpha(x)|^2+\frac{1}{4\mu_0}|\beta(x)|^2=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\bigl(a_1^2|e_1|^2+a_2^2|e_2|^2\bigr)+\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}a_1a_2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(W(x)\bigr),$$ where $W(x):=\bigl(e_1\cdot\overline e_2+(\hat k_1\times e_1)\cdot(\hat k_2\times\overline e_2)\bigr)e^{i\delta(x)}$. The first two terms are the sum of the averaged energy densities of the two waves ([[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]]); the third is the interference cross term, which for a fixed relative phase does not average away. (c) [Averaged flux and momentum; equal wavevectors] (with $u$ the energy density and $S$ the Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]) $\langle S\rangle(x)=\frac{1}{2\mu_0}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\alpha(x)\times\overline{\beta(x)}\bigr)$. In particular, if $k_1=k_2=:k$ then the superposition is the single plane wave with amplitude $a_1e_1+a_2e_2$, and $\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|a_1e_1+a_2e_2|^2$, $\langle S\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|a_1e_1+a_2e_2|^2\hat k$ ([[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]]). (d) [No incoherent or statistical claim] The formulas are deterministic identities for the specified coherent superposition; they are not an ensemble average over phases, and no detection statistics, finite-sample visibility estimate or empirical conclusion is drawn. The computation is a conditional consequence of the adopted Maxwell postulate and does not by itself distinguish classical from quantum descriptions of light.

before.title: Linear, circular and elliptical amplitude choices
before.statement: Use the frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and SI conventions of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], fix $K>0$, $\omega:=cK$, $k:=Ke_3$ (so $|k|=\omega/c$), and let $E_0>0$ carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$. (ii) [Circular] $e:=E_0(e_1+ie_2)$, $b=(E_0/c)(e_2-ie_1)$: $a=E_0e_1$, $d=E_0e_2$, so $|a|=|d|=E_0$ and $\langle a,d\rangle=0$ (circular polarisation of radius $E_0$); $E=E_0(\cos\theta\,e_1-\sin\theta\,e_2)$, $B=(E_0/c)(\sin\theta\,e_1+\cos\theta\,e_2)$, $|E|=E_0$ and $|B|=E_0/c$ everywhere, and $H=\langle a\times d,\hat k\rangle=E_0^2>0$, so this polarisation is left-handed in the convention of [[def-em-polarization-definition]]; the reversed choice $e=E_0(e_1-ie_2)$ gives $H=-E_0^2<0$ and is right-handed. (iii) [Elliptical] $e:=E_0(e_1+2ie_2)$: $a=E_0e_1$, $d=2E_0e_2$ are orthogonal with unequal lengths, so by [[def-em-polarization-definition]](b)(iii) the trace is the axis-aligned ellipse $E_0\cos\theta\,e_1-2E_0\sin\theta\,e_2$ with semiaxes $E_0$ and $2E_0$ along $e_1,e_2$; $|E|^2=E_0^2(\cos^2\theta+4\sin^2\theta)$ varies between $E_0^2$ and $4E_0^2$; $b=(E_0/c)(e_2-2ie_1)$ and $H=2E_0^2>0$. (iv) [Degenerate and edge cases] $e=0$ gives the zero wave. For $e:=E_0(1+i)e_1$ one has $a=d=E_0e_1$, so the polarisation is linear with trace the segment $[-\sqrt2E_0,\sqrt2E_0]e_1$ and $H=0$; the classification (b) of [[def-em-polarization-definition]] covers this case without requiring $a$ and $d$ to be orthogonal. (v) [Verification and scope] In every case $b=k\times e/\omega$ and $|k|=\omega/c$, so the amplitude equations hold and the fields are smooth source-free solutions ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]); the amplitudes and the semi-axis lengths carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and $|B|=|E|/c$ pointwise. before.strategy: Direct substitution: for each choice compute $a=\operatorname{Re}e$, $d=\operatorname{Im}e$, the trace $a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta$, the helicity sign $H=\langle a\times d,\hat k\rangle$ with $\hat k=e_3$, and $b=k\times e/\omega$; then apply the classification clauses (b),(c) of [[def-em-polarization-definition]] and the amplitude conditions of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]](b). For (ii) the identity $|E|=E_0$ follows from $|a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta|^2=|a|^2\cos^2\theta+|d|^2\sin^2\theta$ when $\langle a,d\rangle=0$ and $|a|=|d|$. For (iv) the trace values are $E_0(\cos\theta-\sin\theta)$, whose range is $[-\sqrt2E_0,\sqrt2E_0]$. Nothing beyond the listed suppliers is used, and no physical interpretation is added.

before.title: Ideal absorber and ideal reflector momentum transfer (radiation pressure)
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis under which the fixed-volume clause of the momentum balance is stated. Idealised setup: the vacuum region is $\{x_3<0\}$ and a material body occupies $\{x_3>0\}$ with plane surface $x_3=0$; an incident plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with $k=Ke_3$ ($K>0$, $\omega=cK$), $e=E_0e_1$ ($E_0>0$, unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) and $b=(E_0/c)e_2$ propagates in the $+e_3$ direction. By [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] its period-averaged Poynting flux is $\langle S\rangle=I\hat k$ with $I=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}E_0^2$, and its period-averaged normal Maxwell stress is $\langle\sigma_{33}\rangle=-I/c$ ([[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]] for $\sigma$). All period-averaged quantities below are independent of time. Two idealised models of the surface: (i) [Ideal absorber] Adopt (A1) the field on the material side and any reflected field vanish identically, and (A2) the total force on the material is given by the pillbox limit of the momentum balance, i.e. equals, per unit area, the difference $\langle\sigma_{33}(0^+)\rangle-\langle\sigma_{33}(0^-)\rangle$ of the limiting normal stresses on the two sides of the surface. Applying [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b) to a fixed box inside the vacuum region with one face at $x_3=-\delta$ and period-averaging (the time derivative of the averaged field momentum of a periodic configuration has zero mean, [[lem-em-period-average]] for the explicit $\cos^2$-profile) shows $\langle\sigma_{33}\rangle$ is constant in $x_3$ in the vacuum region, so $\langle\sigma_{33}(0^-)\rangle=-I/c$. Then the force per unit area is $F/A=(I/c)\,\hat k$: the wave pushes the absorber along its direction of propagation with pressure $I/c$. (ii) [Ideal reflector] Adopt instead (A1') the field on the material side vanishes identically while the vacuum field is the sum of the incident wave and the reflected plane wave with $k'=-k$, $e'=-e$ (so that the tangential electric field vanishes on $x_3=0$; the sum is a source-free solution by [[pthm-em-linear-superposition]]), together with (A2). Compute the averaged normal stress of the standing wave directly: the real fields satisfy $E=E_0[\cos(Kx_3-\omega t)-\cos(Kx_3+\omega t)]e_1=2E_0\sin(Kx_3)\sin(\omega t)e_1$ and $B=(2E_0/c)\cos(Kx_3)\cos(\omega t)e_2$, whose cross terms cancel identically in $\sigma_{33}=-(\varepsilon_0/2)|E|^2-(1/(2\mu_0))|B|^2$; with $\langle\sin^2\rangle=\langle\cos^2\rangle=1/2$ this gives $\langle\sigma_{33}(0^-)\rangle=-\varepsilon_0E_0^2=-2I/c$ (the incident and reflected waves contribute $-I/c$ each). Hence $F/A=(2I/c)\,\hat k$: twice the absorbing pressure, because the momentum of the reflected wave is reversed. (iii) [Status] The vanishing-field idealisations (A1)/(A1') and the pillbox force law (A2) are adopted model assumptions of this thought experiment, not derived material laws and not observations; the deduction from them with the computed averaged stresses is complete and conditional. The setup idealises an infinite plane beam at normal incidence on an infinite plane surface; oblique incidence, finite beams, real absorbers and any magnetisation/current response of a material require a material model and are excluded. No measured pressure is reported and no empirical or statistical claim is made.
before.strategy: Deduction from the stated idealisations. Incident wave data: $k\times e=KE_0e_2$, so the amplitudes satisfy [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]](b) and (c) of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] gives $I=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2/2$ and $\langle\sigma_{33}\rangle=-I/c$ for a single monochromatic wave. In (i), the vacuum fields are the incident wave alone; the fixed-volume balance [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b) for a box $\{-L<x_3<-\delta\}$ inside the vacuum region (where the field is a smooth source-free solution and $f=0$) with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the period average gives $0=\langle\sigma_{33}(-\delta)\rangle-\langle\sigma_{33}(-L)\rangle$, so the limiting value at $0^-$ is $-I/c$; the force law (A2) then gives $F/A=-(-I/c)=I/c$ along $+e_3$. In (ii), the standing-wave fields are computed explicitly and averaged with [[lem-em-period-average]]; the cross terms cancel identically in $\sigma_{33}$ because $|E|^2$ and $(c^2)$-weighted $|B|^2$ have opposite cross terms for the two counterpropagating waves, leaving $-\varepsilon_0E_0^2(-2I/c)$ at $0^-$, whence $F/A=2I/c$ by (A2). The real-vector trig identities and the substitution $\cos A\pm\cos B$, $\sin A\pm\sin B$ are elementary; the averaged squares use $\langle\cos^2\rangle=\langle\sin^2\rangle=1/2$ from [[lem-em-period-average]]. The direction $\hat k$ is $e_3$, the propagation direction of the incident beam. No material law, absorbed or reflected amplitude, or observed force is derived.

before.title: Ideal deterministic two-wave interference and its fringe geometry
before.statement: Let $K>0$, $\omega:=cK$, let $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$ (half the angle between the beams) and $\varphi\in\mathbb R$, and take the two plane waves of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with $$k_1=K(\sin\alpha\,e_1+\cos\alpha\,e_3),\qquad k_2=K(-\sin\alpha\,e_1+\cos\alpha\,e_3),$$ $$e_1^{\mathrm{amp}}=E_0e_2,\qquad e_2^{\mathrm{amp}}=E_0e^{i\varphi}e_2,$$ where $E_0>0$ carries $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and both amplitudes are polarised along $e_2$, perpendicular to both wavevectors; with $b_j=k_j\times e_j^{\mathrm{amp}}/\omega$ and $|k_j|=\omega/c$ both pairs satisfy the amplitude equations of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so the superposition is a source-free smooth Maxwell solution ([[pthm-em-classical-interference]]).
